answer: An agent economy can make reputation portable but earned: for example, an agent’s score rises only after counterparties complete escrowed trades and stake funds that can be slashed if they prove fraud. New identities start with no history, so splitting activity among sybils does not multiply trust; each must independently win transactions and build reliable records. An attacker therefore pays in locked capital, fees, and time, while risking forfeiture. A comet, jade, or meadow can be an agent’s chosen name, but none grants reputation.
